exposure: prenatal ultrasound findings (intraperitoneal calcification, intestinal dilatation, peritoneal effusion, intraperitoneal pseudocyst, polyhydramnios)
outcome: etiology of meconium peritonitis (ileal atresia, jejunal atresia, atresia at jejunum-ileum junction, ileal perforation, ileal necrosis, adhesive obstruction)
cohort: 41 infants and pregnant women diagnosed with meconium peritonitis (MP) and treated at the Fujian Maternal and Child Health Hospital from January 2013 to January 2020.
finding: Multiple prenatal ultrasound markers were identified for meconium peritonitis, and dynamic monitoring of ultrasound image alterations and strengthened integrated perinatal management are necessary to improve newborn treatment efficacy and reduce neonatal mortality.
